text:
rachel: noticing a spike in tiny-pod evictions in ap-northeast1 since 07:10 UTC. pending-tiny-pods up 70 -> 420 in 30m. pods report attach timeouts and tail latency degradation.

owen: any node-level hints? conntrack or attach service errors?

rachel: grabbed log from apn-nv-04 at 07:12:
```
Jul 03 07:12:14 kubelet[3011]: attach: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = websocket: close 1006
Jul 03 07:12:15 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
Jul 03 07:12:16 kubelet[3011]: attach: timeout waiting for device attach: context deadline exceeded
Jul 03 07:12:16 kubelet[3011]: evicting pod small-eval-21 due to attach timeout
```

priya: scheduler's anti-affinity + rack spread is scattering 0.25/0.5 GPU tiny pods across racks, increasing attach concurrency and cross-rack egress. we see many 0.5 slots stranded per node in the fragmentation map.

david: infra-bot alert: ap-northeast1 tiny-evict-rate > 60/min (alert infra:tiny-evict:3642).

ops-lead: quick mitigations: 1) soft coalesce scheduler hint to favor nodes with existing tiny pods, 2) warm-pool controller attach-rate limiter + jitter, 3) cautious conntrack bump on a small canary. prefer controller/scheduler changes first.

owen: agree. bumping nf_conntrack fleet-wide is risky. I'll add a per-controller limiter (ATTACH_RATE=12/s) and 50-200ms random backoff. low blast radius and reversible.

priya: i'll prepare a minimal scheduler scoring patch: if pod.resource.gpu <= 0.5 then score += 80 when node.tiny_count > 0, respect tenant anti-affinity. PR link will be in incident doc. This reduces spread without breaking tenant constraints.

rachel: plan for canary rollout: 1) deploy attach-rate-limiter to warm-pool in ap-northeast1-a at 08:00 UTC 2) enable scheduler coalesce on 12 canary nodes (label canary=packtiny) 3) monitor 30m windows for attach-p95, evict-rate, pending-tiny-pods, nf_conntrack_count. rollback if evict-rate > 10/min or attach-p95 > 30s.

david: note: coalescing increases CPU density; watch CPU util and OOMs. cost tradeoff: denser packing likely cheaper than adding warm hosts. capture that in postmortem.

infra-bot: [update] canary started 08:02 UTC. metrics: attach-p95 pre=44s now=19s after 7m. pending-tiny-pods down 29%.

owen: good signal. also adding telemetry hook to record "attach_ops_avoided_by_coalesce" so we can quantify savings per-tenant.

priya: one caveat: coalesce must be opt-in per-namespace initially. some tenants prefer spread for noisy-neighbor isolation. feature-flagging that is straightforward.

ops-lead: include rollback commands in the incident doc and tag canary nodes with canary=attachtest. SLA for canary: evict-rate < 8/min and attach-p95 < 25s within 30m. if threshold breached revert controller env and remove label.

rachel: initial 30m snapshot looks promising; evicts down ~45% and attach-p95 stable <20s. will prepare a follow-up RFC for long-term fixes: attach multiplexing/proxy to reduce websocket churn, and warm-pool attach batching that avoids simultaneous cross-rack attaches.

david: ack. also let's add a short-runbook entry: if tiny-evict-rate spikes, first flip attach-rate limiter, then enable coalesce on a small canary, only if both fail consider conntrack bump on warm-family nodes.

infra-bot: [final] canary window closed 08:35 UTC: evict-rate=5.8/min, attach-p95=18.6s, pending-tiny-pods stable. recommending gradual rollout.

priya: filing PRs and postmortem notes now. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
